intro: The Mental Capacity Act empowers people aged 16 and over to make their own decisions, and protects them when they genuinely cannot.
points: Always assume a person has capacity, and give every practicable help before ever concluding they cannot make a decision.
Capacity is decision-specific and time-specific, so assess it for this decision at this moment, never by age, diagnosis or appearance.
People may make unwise choices; disagreeing with a decision is never proof they lack capacity.
Only when capacity is genuinely lacking, act in the person's best interests, starting from their own wishes, feelings and values.
Use restraint only when necessary and proportionate to prevent harm, choosing the least restrictive option for the shortest time.
Recognise when restrictions become a deprivation of liberty under the acid test, and ensure it is authorised through DoLS.
